title: Roman to Integer
statement_short: Given a Roman numeral string s, convert it to an integer. Roman numerals are represented by seven different symbols, where subtractive combinations occur when a smaller value precedes a larger value.
constraints: 1 <= s.length <= 15, s contains only characters ('I', 'V', 'X', 'L', 'C', 'D', 'M'), s is a valid roman numeral in range [1, 3999]
hint: Extremely small string length (s.length <= 15) allows a single-pass character map lookup with conditional subtraction.
keywords: smaller value precedes a larger value
why_not: Right: Math / Geometry applies numeral symbol values and subtractive rules (subtracting when current symbol < next symbol) in O(n) time. Not HashMap / Hash Set: Using a hash table maps symbols to values, but the core logic is linear arithmetic symbol parsing. Not Stack: Pushing symbols to a stack handles nesting, but simple left-to-right symbol value comparisons require no stack frame. Not Backtracking: Roman numerals follow deterministic grammar rules, requiring no recursive branch search.
